name: Falias
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: One of the four Irish mythological sites that the Tuatha Dé Danann, the people of the goddess Danu, arrived from was Falias. Falias was ruled by Morfessa and was also the origin of the Lia Fáil, which is Ireland’s Inauguration Stone.

okr.objective: Falias is one of the four Irish places from which the Tuatha Dé Danann came.
key_results: Falias was one of the four sites where the Tuatha Dé Danann, the people of the goddess Danu, originated.
Morfessa ruled as lord of ranks of Falias.
The Lia Fáil, Ireland's Inauguration Stone, came from Falias.
The Tuatha Dé Danann reached Ireland from Falias or its sister cities.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
